Write-Permission Gap (johnangelol 403s)

johnangelol 403s on all write operations (dept/job-title/work-location creates, edits, deactivates). TC-028 (create) shows inline error correctly. TC-044 (Settings save) and TC-056 (deactivate) fail silently -- no error toast, no user feedback. Silent-403 pattern on Settings sub-tab and kebab deactivate vs explicit inline error on modal create is an inconsistent UX bug.

Silent-403 UX Bug (TC-044 / TC-056): TC-044 and TC-056 surface silent 403s (no toast, Save button stays active after 403). TC-028 correctly shows inline "You don't have permission to do that." Inconsistent error handling for write operations across modal vs Settings sub-tab paths.

Verdict: FAILED -- 3 genuine product defects found. Module is deployed and core functionality (create, edit, deactivate 0-member dept, tab navigation, entity switch, stats bar, duplicate-name warning, discard confirm, province list) works. Blockers: 45 TCs blocked by missing test data (no employees, no granular-permission users provisioned); 28 API TCs deferred (API key not configured, endpoints undocumented).

Pass rate among executed TCs: 27/51 = 53%

Defects (3)

#1 SN-14-FE001 NOT FILED P1

SN-14-FE001 -- Inactive department rows fully disabled; Reactivate kebab unreachable

After deactivating a department, the table row gains aria-disabled="true" and the kebab button becomes [disabled]. Spec AC-OD4 requires a "Reactivate" option in the kebab menu for inactive records. With the row and button disabled, there is no interactive path to reactivate a department from the UI. Playwright cannot click the disabled button (timeout). The deactivation itself works correctly (TC-057 PASS) but reactivation is blocked.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-059 -- Reactivate record -- no confirm, immediate, toast (primary)
  • TC-065 -- Reactivate -- (inactive) labels auto-revert on Employee Profile
  • TC-087 -- Reactivate department -- inactive employee labels revert automatically

Spec refs

AC-OD4, [ORG-6.13.1]

Evidence

#2 SN-14-FE002 NOT FILED P2

SN-14-FE002 -- Province dropdown sorted by code not name_en; bilingual display absent

Two related issues on the Province dropdown: (1) The list is sorted by TH province code (Bangkok TH-10 first, numeric order) rather than alphabetically by English name. Spec TC-104 requires sort by name_en ascending ("Amnat Charoen" should be first). (2) Province options display English name + province code (e.g., "Bangkok TH-10") but do NOT show the Thai-script name (name_th). Spec ORG-7.3.2 / Sec 16 requires bilingual display for TH province options.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-104 -- Province dropdown -- sorts by name_en in Phase 1 (primary)
  • TC-039 -- Province dropdown options show bilingual labels (English + Thai name)
  • TC-038 -- 77-province dropdown (UI portion -- count PASS; bilingual and sort FAIL)

Spec refs

TC-104, ORG-7.3.2, Sec 16, OQ-ORG2, E-8

Evidence

#3 SN-14-FE003 NOT FILED P3

SN-14-FE003 -- Job Title create modal label reads "Name *" instead of "Title name" (AC-OC5 deviation)

The Add Job Title modal renders the name input field label as "Name *". Spec AC-OC5 / [ORG-7.2.1] specifies the label MUST read "Title name" with no English-language qualifier such as "(English)". This is a copy/label deviation -- the field label is incorrect per spec.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-030 -- Job Title create modal name label reads "Title name" with no qualifier (primary)

Spec refs

AC-OC5, [ORG-7.2.1]

Evidence
